How much does it cost to run a dehumidifier?

Compressor dehumidifiers are fairly cheap to run. Desiccant models use more power but also give off some useful heat.

Cost per day
53p
About £95.80 a year at 8 hours per day, 7 days a week, 6 months a year.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

A typical dehumidifier uses about 250 watts (150–700W depending on the model). Used for 8 hours per day, 7 days a week, for 6 months of the year, it costs about 53p per day and £95.80 a year at the current price cap rate.

Worth knowing: CSE lists dehumidifier 500W.

Source for the typical figure: Typical range (estimate). See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Set a target humidity (around 50%) rather than running it flat out.
  • Run it in a closed room for best results.
  • Placing it near drying laundry is often cheaper than a tumble dryer.

Questions

How much does it cost to run a dehumidifier per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 250W model costs about 6.6p an hour while it's running.

How much does it cost to run a dehumidifier per year?

About £95.80 a year, based on 8 hours per day, 7 days a week, 6 months a year. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my dehumidifier's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
